cross-toxin: donor toxin is ImI (P50983), not RgIA, on Ac-AChBP. Donor and target toxins share the measured Cys framework (inter-Cys gaps 0/4/3, alpha4/3) but differ in sequence, and the receptors are different proteins.  Built because the tier-1 6HY7<-7EGR set encloses 100 % of 6HY7's native contacts

cross-toxin, cross-framework: donor toxin OmIA is 18 aa with inter-Cys gaps 0/4/7 (alpha4/7) vs RgIA 0/4/3 (alpha4/3), and the receptor is Ls-AChBP (P58154).  The most distant donor available; included as the strict/stress variant
cross-toxin: donor toxin ImI on human alpha7.  Unlike 6HY7 this donor has both (+) and (-) chains, so 7EGR gets a two-face set
cross-toxin: donor toxin RgIA on Ac-AChBP
cross-toxin: donor toxin RgIA on human alpha9; (+) face only because the donor receptor is a single subunit

no second LvIA entry exists in this set.  Donor differs in BOTH toxin (OmIA) and receptor species (Ls-AChBP P58154 vs Ac-AChBP Q8WSF8) -- strictly harder than same-toxin.  Chosen over the ImI/RgIA donors because donor and target toxins share the measured Cys spacing / loop-2 length (gaps 0/4/7, see cys_framework)
reciprocal; donor LvIA/Ac-AChBP, different toxin and species, same measured Cys framework (0/4/7)

no second GIC entry exists.  Donor OmIA/Ls-AChBP differs in toxin and in receptor species, and shares the measured Cys framework.  A 5XGL donor would have been same-receptor (Ac-AChBP) and so a weaker test of the transplant

Cross-toxin (ImI, alpha4/3, gaps 0/4/3) vs target LvIA (alpha4/7, gaps 0/4/7); same receptor protein Ac-AChBP so residue mapping is near-identity and the test is purely 'does a 4/3 toxin footprint predict a 4/7 toxin footprint'
